issues.defect: UndoneAt is written unconditionally, even when entries failed. Failure causes include access denied on C:\Users\Public\Desktop in the documented non-elevated direct run '-DesktopIconAction Undo', or a locked file. After that the default undo skips this run and replays the older run out of order, and the explicit -DesktopIconUndoManifest path stops at line 1806 with 'Already undone'. The failed entries can never be retried with the tool.
issues.fix: Set UndoneAt (and rewrite the manifest) only when $undoResults.Errors.Count -eq 0. Otherwise leave it empty and print that a rerun retries the failed entries. A rerun is already safe: moves only run when Destination exists and Source is free, copies and links only when present, and mkdir only when empty.

issues.defect: $Global:DESKTOP_BACKUP_DIR.TrimEnd('\') + '\' builds a path prefix by appending a string to a variable. AGENTS.md, the shell-windows role rule and the file's own header rule 6 forbid this.

A copy-mode shortcut (Chrome/Edge) with the same name on both the user and the Public desktop but with different content makes each run displace the other copy. That writes a manifest on every run, which is not idempotent. This machine does not have that layout.
issues.fix: Plan at most one item per destination path and report the later ones as conflicts.

issues.defect: Get-Item $targetPath still lacks -LiteralPath, so names containing [ ] fail silently.

The rule that copies Chrome/Edge into Browsers and keeps them on the desktop is behavior, not a Windows format, yet it sits in the platform-only row. The SPW-001 request also does not point shell-linux at the existing scripts/shells/linux/common/desktop_shortcut_manager.sh helpers _dsm_login_users and _dsm_desktop_dir.
issues.fix: Move the browser keep-copy rule into the SPW-001 request, or give the reason Linux differs. Ask shell-linux to reuse the _dsm_* helpers instead of new desktop-dir discovery.
